title: optimize-evals-1on1-prep-quality-regressions-ab-notes
content:
Meeting: 1:1 with Samir (optimize lead) - prep notes
Date: 2026-03-26
Location: Zoom / async sync
Goal: quick status on active eval regressions, review A/B run results from last deploy, align on next steps for prompt set pruning and canary rollout for quantized model.

Topline summary:
- Two small but visible quality regressions surfaced in v3.2.1 canary (mostly hallucination on entity recall and list completion).
- A/B run (v3.2.0 baseline vs v3.2.1 canary) shows ~4.8% drop in top-1 factual accuracy on our core QA prompt set (prompt-set-core-v2).
- Latency & cost metrics: 5% lower token cost using new batching strategy + quantized runtime path, latency within SLO for 95th pctl.
- Hypothesis: change in decoder sampling tweaks + new prompt normalization step introduced in tokenizer patch caused tokenization boundary shifts for some entity-rich prompts.

Data / Evidence to bring to the 1:1:
- Eval summary (quick bullets):
  * prompt-set-core-v2: baseline acc 84.3% -> canary 79.5% (absolute -4.8)
  * prompt-set-list-generation-v1: BLEU-like score down ~3.1 points, truncation on long lists noted
  * Safety/regression set: no increase in toxicity flags
  * Latency: p95 baseline 210ms -> canary 225ms (within target)
  * Cost: per-token exec cost -5% (win)
- Samples: 6 representative failures saved under s3://redwood-evals/optimize/taylor/fail-samples/ (ids listed in linked_artifacts)
- Diff in tokenization: attached sample showing whitespace normalization causing extra token split on product names (e.g., "X-1000" -> "X-", "1000")

Immediate hypotheses / things to check quickly during sync:
- Roll back tokenizer patch vs revert decoder sampling change (which is more likely cause?)
- Run targeted eval on only tokenizer change and only sampling change (isolated A/B) - quick smoke run on 2k prompts
- Check whether KV-cache alignment could be impacted by new prompt prefix trimming logic

Proposed near-term plan (options + recommendation):
1) Quick mitigation (recommended initial step): revert tokenizer normalization in runtime and re-run core evals overnight; if regression disappears, schedule a targeted PR that preserves normalization for safety-critical inputs only.
   - Pros: fast, likely to remove entity splitting issue
   - Cons: loses some normalization benefits (but we can whitelist)
2) Canary rollback of sampling tweak only (if tokenization check inconclusive).
3) Keep canary but add prompt rewrite layer for problematic prompts (short-term band-aid).

Action items to propose and assign in 1:1:
- Taylor: run isolated A/B (tokenizer-only vs baseline) and collect metrics (due 2026-03-27) [JIRA: OPT-789]
- Samir: prioritize hotfix review if tokenizer revert looks good; coordinate with release-eng for rapid canary replace (due 2026-03-28)
- Jamie: craft short internal note for customer-success (CS) if rollback planned - include mitigations and timeline (due 2026-03-28)
- Infra: warm up cache for canary nodes once new build deployed (contact infra on slack #deploys)

Questions to ask Samir (priority order):
- Do we prefer an immediate revert if tokenizer isolation shows signal, or do we want more triage to be 100% sure before reverting?
- Is there appetite to accept the small factual accuracy hit for the cost win in the short term? (I'd recommend no for core customers)
- Can release-eng support a same-day canary swap if needed?

Open notes / rough debugging log (scratchpad):
- 2026-03-24 09:12: reproducer_run_001: saw entity split in ~12/200 samples
- 2026-03-24 11:03: tried reverting prompt normalization locally -> sample passes, need larger run
- 2026-03-25 16:40: A/B aggregated metrics uploaded to s3, delta table at gs://redwood-evals/deltas/2026-03-25.csv
- Observed oddity: list-gen prompts with trailing punctuation more likely to truncate

Notes for follow-up (post 1:1):
- If Samir wants revert: create PR draft with revert + test cases (Taylor)
- If keep canary: add additional eval slices and increase canary sample size by 3x for next 48h (Ops)

Misc / background context to have ready:
- Linked confluence page with eval methodology: confluence:OPTIMIZE-EVALS-2026
- Recent PRs touching tokenizer/sampling: github:pull/1234, github:pull/1229
- Customer reports: cs-ticket-4412 (customer A reported hallucination on product specs)

Quick TL;DR to paste into Slack if needed:
"Found a ~5% drop in factual accuracy in v3.2.1 canary likely tied to recent tokenizer normalization. Cost improved ~5%. I recommend a targeted tokenizer revert smoke test tonight; if signal holds, fast revert + hotfix. Will run tokenizer-only A/B and share results by EOD 3/27."

TODO (personal):
- prep the 2k-smoke eval job and ensure it uses isolated commit hashes for tokenizer/sampling
- snapshot current canary model artifacts and log exact image tags
- add test cases to repo: tests/evals/tokenization_regressions.test

End of notes
